__ 1. Implementation

The document has been created and approved by the General Assembly of 09.11.2024.
The document and its rules have been implemented since the 2025 season.

2. Definition

“Tabard” is a generic term used to describe the cloth worn upon the armor. It is made to show the heraldry
of the wearer and prove your wealth and status on the battlefield, or in the list.
Nowadays, Tabards have the same function as a sports jersey: to indicate the team you belong to.

Type of Tabards:

● Sleeveless Tabard
Tabards without sleeves. Simple design, common in the 13th century and 14th century. Tend
to be rare in the 15th century.

● Short-sleeves Tabard
Tabards with short sleeves that can go up to the elbow. Common design in the 14th century.
Tend to be rare in the 15th century.

● Long-sleeves Tabard
Tabards with long sleeves that cover the whole arms, from shoulder to hand. Common
design in the 14th and the 15th century.

● Eastern Tabard
We do not have many historical references for eastern Tabard. It is allowed to use the same
Tabard as European armors. Eastern stylization of Tabard are displayed in the document
“Eastern Armors’”.

● Exception for full plates armors
Wearing full plates armor makes the use of Tabard not practical. Therefore, it is allowed to
wear only a scarf. Scarves must follow the General Requirements (see section 3 below).

__ 3. General Requirements

3.1. Material Requirements

All Tabards and Scarves must respect the following requirements:

● Shapes, decorations and designs must be based on historical sources.
● Tabards must conform to the “Textiles and Leather” document.
● Tabards can be made of the following materials:

○ wool,
○ linen,
○ Silk,

○  coton,

○ any other material based on historical sources.

● Tabards can be made of modern materials in the following cases:
○ the modern material replicates the aesthetic of an approved material listed above,
○ the modern material is strong enough to endure full contact fights and to not be damaged
too easily,
○ we recommend asking for approval of the Authenticity Committee regarding Tabard
made of modern materials before placing an order.

3.2. Fastening Systems Requirements

Tabards can be tied with the following systems:

● buttons made of fabric, wood, bone, or metal,

● laces, made of leather, rope or fabric,

● any other system based on historical sources,

● any modern fastening system is denied. (Zips, snap buttons, velcro, paracord, nylon rope
etc.).

Tabards can be open on the side, tied with laces.
Tabards can be open on the front, and tied with buttons.

3.3. Colors Requirements

Colors used for Tabards must be based on historical sources. Any clearly modern color is denied. (Neon
pink, fluorescent yellow, etc.)

For the Marshals’ safety, the use of yellow as a main color of a Tabard is Denied. Yellow color must
represent less than 50% of the Tabard colors. The combination of black and yellow must not be inspired
by Marshal’s uniforms.

3.4. Symbols and Decorations Requirements

Symbols and decorations used for Tabards must be based on historical sources. Any clearly modern
symbol or decoration is denied. (Warhammer logo, movies or TV show imagery, modern slogan etc.)

We recommend taking inspiration from middle ages manuscripts to create your symbols.
Symbols and decorations used for Tabards must be made with the following techniques:

● embroidery,

● painting: can be by hand or by stamp,

● sewing a patchwork of clothes to create a design,
● any other techniques based on historical sources.

3.5. Exception for Cuirass

When wearing a Cuirass, it is allowed to wear the Tabard under it. In this case, it is also allowed to wear
the pauldrons upon the Tabard.

4. Sleeveless Tabard

4.1. Historical Sources and Datation

Sleeveless Tabard is an easy way to display your heraldic. This type of Tabard has been used all along
the Middle Ages, from knight templars to late 15th century armors.

They are Approved for 14th century, Transitional and 15th century armors.

Life of Eustace and Other Saints - 1300 - France Weltchronik - 1360 - Germany Bibliothéque de Besancon - 1410 - France

4.2. Specific Requirements

Sleeveless Tabard must:

● follow the General Requirements (see Section 3 above),
● not be too long, Knee is the limit.

5. Short-sleeves Tabard

5.1. Historical Sources and Datation

Short-sleeves Tabard is the main design of the 14th century and later. Its simple shape makes it easy to
craft and to wear. Many different designs can be documented by historical sources

They are Approved for 14th century, Transitional and 15th century armors.

Bible historiale - 1360 - France Weltchronik - 1360 - Germany Office of the Feast of Corpus Christi - 1403 - Austria

5.2. Specific Requirements

Short-sleeves Tabard must:
● follow the General Requirements (see Section 3 above),
● not be too long, Knee is the limit,
● not have sleeves too long. Elbow is the limit, unless it can be documented by historical
sources.
● have open or plain (as a shirt) sleeves.

6. Long-Sleeves Tabard

6.1. Historical Sources and Datation

Long-sleeves Tabard combine the role of exposing your heraldry and protecting your armor. The sleeves
often cover the whole arm, up to the wrist, but can be shorter (up to mid-forearm). Many different designs
can be documented by historical sources.

They are Approved for 14th century, Transitional and 15th century armors.

6.2. Specific Requirements

Long-sleeves Tabard must:

● follow the General Requirements (see Section 3 above),

● not be too long, Knee is the limit,

● cover the arm up to the middle of the forearm as a minimum,
● have plain (as a shirt) sleeves.
